Here we quantify, using Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 5 global climate model simulations calibrated to remove spatial biases, how projected sea ice loss might increase opportunities for Arctic transit shipping. By midcentury for standard open water vessels, the frequency of navigable periods doubles, with routes across the central Arctic becoming available. A sea ice\u2010ship speed relationship is used to show that European routes to Asia typically become 10\u2009days faster via the Arctic than alternatives by midcentury, and 13\u2009days faster by late century, while North American routes become 4\u2009days faster. Future greenhouse gas emissions have a larger impact by late century; the shipping season reaching 4\u20138\u2009months in Representative Concentration Pathway (RCP)8.5 double that of RCP2.6, both with substantial interannual variability. Moderately, ice\u2010strengthened vessels likely enable Arctic transits for 10\u201312\u2009months by late
